look_here_first: FIRST photograph the UPPER FACE of an actual mature leaf or white-margined BRACT. *Euphorbia marginata* usually has a GLABROUS (mostly smooth, hairless) UPPER blade; stems, peduncles, lower midribs and capsules may STILL be hairy. Second, compare the LARGEST fully developed showy BRACTS: usually relatively BROAD elliptic/obovate rather than the very long linear-to-narrowly-oblanceolate bracts of *E. bicolor*. Both species can look just as white, and smaller secondary bracts of *marginata* may be narrow. 'More frosting' or 'even white borders' is NOT a reliable field key. What looks like large white flower petals are white-margined MODIFIED LEAVES (bracts), along with small white cyathial-gland appendages. Hays/Travis/Kerr project native-range PASS stays in place.

key_traits.label: Family pattern
key_traits.text: Euphorbia: milky latex and a cyathium instead of an ordinary petaled flower. The conspicuous white areas are primarily bracts plus gland appendages.

key_traits.label: Growth form
key_traits.text: Annual, erect herb with a conspicuously white-topped flowering canopy.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Distal leaves and bracts become conspicuously white-margined; the showiest upper bracts are relatively broad.

key_traits.label: Pubescence
key_traits.text: Upper leaf surfaces are mostly glabrous. Hairiness can still occur on lower surfaces, along the midrib, peduncles, cyathia, ovary, and capsule, so 'the whole plant is hairless' is not a safe rule.

key_traits.label: Bracts
key_traits.text: Largest white-margined bracts are generally broader, commonly elliptic to obovate, rather than the long narrow linear-to-narrowly-oblanceolate bracts of E. bicolor.

key_traits.label: Cyathium
key_traits.text: Flower-like cyathia bear pale glands with conspicuous white appendages.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Three-lobed capsule, conspicuously hairy; detailed Williamson treatment gives capsules about 4.5–5 × 7–7.5 mm.

key_traits.label: Seed
key_traits.text: Seeds about 4.5 × 3 mm in the detailed Williamson treatment, with minute tuberculate/netlike surface patterning.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Native to target zone under existing Hays, Travis and Kerr county records; no need to change this project's PASS.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Annual erect/taprooted plant, white-topped canopy, often 30–85 cm; height does not separate it from *E. bicolor*.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Stem leaves alternate and relatively BROAD ovate to elliptic; showiest distal white-margined bracts mostly elliptic to obovate rather than extremely slender.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Upper faces of mature leaves/bracts commonly GLABROUS, even when the stem or under-leaf midrib has hairs.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Smaller inner inflorescence bracts CAN be narrow; don't ID by one tiny secondary bract.

lookalikes.differences: Against E. bicolor, use two linked characters: E. marginata is generally broader-bracted and glabrous on the upper leaf/bract surfaces; E. bicolor is narrower-bracted and conspicuously hairy above.
